name: Crane Venture Partners
identity_check: Confirmed as Crane Venture Partners (crane.vc, also just 'Crane'), the early-stage VC co-founded in London in 2015 by Krishna Visvanathan and Scott Sage (crane.vc Our Story and Team pages). It invests from inception through seed; its September 2026 announcement ($484M across Crane III, Crane APAC I, Crane US I and Crane Opportunity Fund I) appears on crane.vc and in MassMutual Ventures' copy of the release. MassMutual Ventures (MMV) has been a minority owner and anchor LP since 2018, and since 2025 Crane administers MMV's ~$450M Europe/APAC funds. Those MMV vehicles are not Crane's own funds and are not recorded as funds here. Not MassMutual Ventures itself, not Crane Co. / Crane NXT (US industrial companies), and not any other firm using 'Crane' in its name. The $150M 'Q3 2026 fund close' lead (read from a treemap logo) matches Crane APAC I. The $484M lead is the total across all four vehicles.

open_items: The original GlobeNewswire release for the $484M raise (2026-09-15) returned HTTP 403. Fund sizes come from MassMutual Ventures' copy of the release and Crane's own 21 Sep 2026 post.

The 2026 fund close dates are the announcement date (2026-09-15). First and final close dates for Crane III, APAC I, US I and Opportunity Fund I are not published. Pulse 2.0 says more than 70% of the $484M was being announced publicly for the first time.

Fund I: the close month (June 2019) comes from a Global Venturing article dated 2019-06-14 reporting the final close 'on Tuesday'. Fund II ($140M): no official vehicle name or close date was found; the date used is the announcement month (May 2022). Fund currencies are as reported (USD).

The MassMutual Ventures Europe and APAC funds (~$450M, 40 portfolio companies) have been administered by Crane since the 2025 agreement. They are MMV vehicles, so they are not recorded as Crane funds.
Check size ($500K–$5M) comes only from Tech Funding News, which attributes it to Crane's website. No crane.vc page fetched states a check size.

There is no dedicated pitch or application form. The application_url is crane.vc's general contact form ('Send us a message'), and the site says 'We don't wait for founders to find us. We go to them.' Cold inbound is inferred from the Kurrent/Event Store post, where a cold email led to Crane leading Event Store's first institutional round (2022).
No page states whether Crane requires a US entity. 'No' is inferred from Crane-led or Crane-backed rounds in French (pyannoteAI) and Dutch (Nopan, Silverflow) companies.

Indian founders: 'yes' is based on India being named among the four investment regions, the Bangalore office and India-based investors (Anandamoy Roychowdhary, Sidhant Goyal). No India-specific round was verified.

Atomic Tessellator A$11.3M seed (Crane-led): the announcement date and co-investors are not stated. The crane.vc post date (10 July 2026) is a bulk re-upload date shared by several older posts. The original announcement is a LinkedIn post, which was not fetched.

OLIX: '$3.3bn valuation' is not labelled pre- or post-money, so valuation_post_original was left null. The earlier OLIX $220M raise (Crane post; FT link paywalled) has no date or investor list on any readable page, so it was skipped.

Chiral $12M (GlobeNewswire 2026-02-06) and Hacktron $2.9M pre-seed (GlobeNewswire 2026-05-13; DevOps.com) returned 403. Crane's posts do not name co-investors or state Crane's role in those rounds, so both were skipped. Chiral's About page shows Crane, Founderful, Quanto Nation and hcvc logos only.

Gable Series A (Crane-led, March 2025): the amount and co-investors are not stated on Crane's post, so it was skipped. ConfigHub stage is taken from the crane.vc portfolio tag (Pre-Seed); the post itself only says 'first $4M'.
Encord Series C: the date is the month of the Tech Funding News article (2026-02-26), which says the round was 'recently raised'. The exact announcement date was not confirmed.

The crane.vc portfolio lists industrial and robotics companies relevant to our sectors: Armatrix (robotic welding, maintenance and inspection), Peppermint Robotics, Gridfield (AI accelerator clusters), ePlane, DePoly, H2Site, Puralink and Pinaca Labs. No round page naming Crane was found for any of them, partly because the shared web-search budget ran out mid-research.

Max Chapman, Dan Jaeck and Sidhant Goyal are labelled 'Investor' on the team cards but 'Principal' in their bios; Sam Kester is a 'Senior Associate' in his bio. Partner sector focus is inferred from bio text, some of which describes prior roles.

Founding years were not found for IMMIX, Expanse, Nopan, Aseon Labs, Bluefish, Encord, SRE.ai/Laminar, Memories.ai, ConfigHub or Atomic Tessellator. HQ was not found for Expanse ('U.S. and U.K.-based'), SRE.ai, Memories.ai, ConfigHub or Atomic Tessellator. For pyannoteAI, Tech Funding News says 'Juan Coria founded pyannoteAI in 2024', which conflicts with the founders Crane names, so no founding year was recorded.
